ControlCaseDef.description: Definition for a single case in a match control construct

default.description: Mark this case as the default/fallback
default.title: Default

body.description: Tasks to execute if this case matches
body.title: Body

ControlCaseDef.title: ControlCaseDef

type.description: Control flow type: if, match, while, do-while, or repeat

until.description: Early exit condition for do-while/repeat loops
until.title: Until

max_iter.title: Max Iter

ExampleDef.description:
A worked example of using a task.

Examples are documentation, not tests: nothing runs them, and nothing
checks that `code` still works. They are deliberately NOT inherited along
the `uses:` chain -- an example is written against a specific task name and
a specific set of parameters, so re-presenting a base task's example under
a derived task would show the reader something they cannot type.

title.description: Short heading for the example (e.g. "Run a single test")
title.title: Title

code.description: The example itself: a shell command line, a YAML fragment, or whatever the reader would actually type
code.title: Code

caption.description: Prose shown with the example, explaining what it does or when to reach for it
caption.title: Caption

lang.description: Language of 'code', used for syntax highlighting. Use 'shell' for command lines, 'yaml' for flow-file fragments
lang.title: Lang

ExampleDef.title: ExampleDef

task.description: Name of the task to extend
task.title: Task

with.description: Parameter modifications to apply to the task
with.title: With

uses.description: Name of the extension to use as a base
uses.title: Uses

FilterDef.description:
Package-level filter definition.

Filters enable reusable data transformations in expressions:
    ${{ inputs | filter_name(arg1, key: val) }}

Visibility control matches task visibility:
- name: Default visibility (visible within package and to root)
- local: Fragment-only filter
- export: Visible to downstream packages
- root: Root package only

name.description: The name of the filter (default visibility)
name.title: Filter Name

root.description: The name of the filter (marked as root scope)
root.title: Root Filter Name

export.description: The name of the filter (marked as export scope)
export.title: Export Filter Name

local.description: The name of the filter (marked as local scope)
local.title: Local Filter Name

scope.description: Visibility scope: 'root', 'export', 'local', or list of package names
scope.title: Filter visibility scope

with.description: Filter parameters. Keys are parameter names, values are ParamDef specifications
with.title: With

desc.description: Short description of the filter's purpose
desc.title: Filter description

shell.description: Interpreter for 'run' implementation (bash, python, python3, etc.)
shell.title: Shell

OverrideDef.description:
Override definition for task or package substitution.

Exactly one of 'task', 'package', or 'override' (deprecated) must be set.

task.description: Fully-qualified name of task to override
task.title: Task

with.description: Replacement task name (str) or inline task definition (dict)
with.title: With

OverrideDef.title: OverrideDef

doc.description: Full documentation of the package. Where 'desc' is the one-line summary shown in listings, this is the prose a reader arriving at the package needs: what it is for and where to start.
doc.title: Doc

type.description: (Deprecated, and inert) Nothing reads this field: data types are declared with 'types:'. It is retained only so that flow files setting it continue to load
type.title: Type

tasks.description: List of tasks defined in the package
tasks.title: Tasks

filters.description: List of filters defined in the package. Filters are reusable data transformations usable in expressions
filters.title: Filters

imports.description: List of packages to import. Can be package names (strings) or import specifications with configuration
imports.title: Imports

package-map.description: One or more package-map files (name -> flow file) consulted when resolving imports by name
package-map.title: Package-Map

overrides.description: Task overrides. Maps target task name to a replacement task name (str) or an inline task definition (dict)
overrides.title: Overrides

fragments.description: List of fragment file paths to include in this package
fragments.title: Fragments

types.description: List of data type definitions for this package
types.title: Types

uses.description: Name of a base package to inherit from. This package extends the base package's tasks and types
uses.title: Uses

tags.description: Tags as type references with optional parameter overrides
tags.title: Tags

from.description: Package identifier or file path to import
from.title: From

as.description: Alias name for the imported package
as.title: As

config.description: Configuration name to apply when importing
config.title: Config

with.description: Parameter overrides to apply to the imported package
with.title: With

type.description: Parameter type (e.g., 'str', 'int', 'bool', 'list', 'map', or a complex type definition)
type.title: Type

append.description: Value to append to list-type parameters
append.title: Append

prepend.description: Value to prepend to list-type parameters
prepend.title: Prepend

path-append.description: Path to append to path-type parameters (OS-specific separator)
path-append.title: Path-Append

path-prepend.description: Path to prepend to path-type parameters (OS-specific separator)
path-prepend.title: Path-Prepend

anyOf.description: Closed set: the accepted values, each either a bare value or {value: v, desc: ...}
{of: [...], open: true} -- an open set warns on an unlisted value instead of failing

values.description: The set of values this parameter accepts. Either a plain list ([a, b, c] -- closed) or {of: [...], open: true}. List elements may be bare values or {value: v, desc: ...}.

anyOf.description: true exposes the parameter as --<name>; false removes a flag inherited via `uses:`
{name, short, hidden} -- rename the flag, add a short option, or keep it out of help

cli.description: Expose this parameter as a command-line option under 'dfm run'. `true` uses the parameter's own name ('build' -> --build); the map form adds a short option, renames the flag, or hides it. `false` removes a flag inherited from a base task. Type, default, help and accepted values all come from this declaration, so there is nothing to restate.
cli.title: Cli

SelectDef.description:
A family of independently-addressable variants of one artifact.

Where `matrix:` fans a task out -- running it runs every cell -- `select:`
declares a *catalog*: each cell is a first-class task named
`<family>.<key>`, built only when something asks for it, and shared when two
consumers ask for the same one.

axes.description: The dimensions of the family. An axis value is a list, or a `${{ }}` expression over PACKAGE variables that resolves to one. Unlike a matrix axis this is resolved at load (cells are declared tasks), so it may not depend on a `set:`/`let` rebind -- a family's shape must not vary by instantiation site.
axes.title: Axes

key.description: Template naming a cell, evaluated against that cell's axis bindings (e.g. "${{ this.view }}-${{ this.build }}"). Defaults to the axis values joined with '.', in declaration order.
key.title: Key

default.description: What the bare family name means: a binding map (the family is an alias for one cell -- values may be `${{ }}` expressions over the task's own parameters), 'all' (a gate over every cell), or 'none' (only cells are addressable). Omitted means the first value of each axis.
default.title: Default

SelectDef.title: SelectDef

chain.description: Enable chain strategy: run body tasks sequentially with each consuming output of previous task
chain.title: Chain

generate.description: Enable generate strategy: dynamically create tasks by running a shell command that outputs task definitions

matrix.description: Matrix of parameter values to explore. Creates one task instance per combination of values. An axis value may be a `${{ }}` expression that resolves to a list (e.g. `image: "${{ images }}"`), evaluated at graph-build.
matrix.title: Matrix

select.description: Enable select strategy: declare a family of independently-addressable variants (`<family>.<key>`) instead of a fan-out. Use `matrix:` when running the task should run every cell; use `select:` when the cells are separate artifacts and asking for one must not build the others.

body.description: Body tasks for strategy execution. Used with chain and matrix strategies
body.title: Body

builtin.description: Name of a built-in summary renderer. Currently: 'task-summary'
builtin.title: Builtin

TaskDef.description: Holds definition information (ie the YAML view) for a task

root.description: The name of the task (marked as root scope)
root.title: Root Task Name

export.description: The name of the task (marked as export scope)
export.title: Export Task Name

local.description: The name of the task (marked as local scope)
local.title: Local Task Name

override.description: The name of the task to override
override.title: Overide Name

uses.description: Task from which this task is derived
uses.title: Base type

iff.description: Condition that must be true for this task to run
iff.title: Task enable condition

shell.description: Shell to use for shell-based implementation
shell.title: Shell

abstract.description: Abstract task: may only be reached via 'uses:' or as an override replacement, never invoked directly
abstract.title: Abstract

elaborate.description: Python callable ('module:function') that elaborates this task type at graph-build time, replacing the default node interior. Signature: elaborate(ctxt, task, name) -> TaskNode. Bound along the 'uses' chain (nearest declaration wins).
elaborate.title: Elaborate

summary.description: End-of-run summary for this task when it is the task being run. Either a Python callable ('module:function') receiving a summary context and returning a renderable/str/None, or {builtin: task-summary}. Bound along the 'uses' chain (nearest declaration wins, whole-value replacement).
summary.title: Summary

control.description: Runtime control flow definition (mutually exclusive with strategy)

desc.description: Short description of the task's purpose
desc.title: Task description

examples.description: Worked examples of using this task. Not inherited along 'uses': an example names a specific task and specific parameters, so a base task's example would not be something a reader of the derived task could type.
examples.title: Examples

needs.description: List of tasks that this task depends on
needs.title: Needs

feeds.description: List of tasks that depend on this task (inverse of needs)
feeds.title: Feeds

let.description: (DEPRECATED — use 'set') Scoped variables provided to this task's subtree, read via resolve(). Does not set this task's own parameters (see 'with').
let.title: Let

set.description: Scoped overrides applied to this task's subtree: a list whose items are either assignment maps ({name: value}) that rebind scoped variables read via ${{ pkg.var }}, or scope items ({uses?, path?, set: [...]}) that narrow/force by matcher. Outer overrides inner; CLI (-D) is the ceiling.
set.title: Set

rundir.description: Specifies handling of this tasks's run directory

passthrough.description: Specifies whether this task should pass its inputs to its output
passthrough.title: Passthrough

consumes.description: Specifies matching patterns for parameter sets that this task consumes
consumes.title: Consumes

produces.description:
Patterns describing the data items this task MAY produce. 'May', not 'always': a conditional output is still worth declaring, and every consumer treats the declaration as what could be produced rather than a guarantee. Declare what this task ADDS -- items it merely passes through are already declared by whatever produced them. `type:` is the item type; other keys are attributes a consumer can match on, and may reference this task's parameters (`filetype: "${{ type }}"`). Inherited along 'uses' with the nearest declaration winning.

`doc:` is the exception: it is prose describing the specific artifact (`doc: "${{ task_rundir }}/ral_pkg.sv"`), not an attribute. It never participates in matching, and it is NOT evaluated -- the shape of the path is what documents the output, where one machine's resolution of it is not.
produces.title: Produces

uptodate.description: Up-to-date check: false=always run, string=Python method, None=use default check
uptodate.title: Uptodate

cache.description: Cache configuration. True=enabled with defaults, False=disabled, CacheDef=custom config
cache.title: Cache

tags.description: Tags as type references with optional parameter overrides
tags.title: Tags

requires.description: Contract this task must satisfy: a list of check-type references with optional parameter overrides (the same shape as 'tags'). Evaluated at graph build against every node built from this task, AFTER override resolution -- so a requirement declared by a base task is what a project overriding it must satisfy. Accumulated along the 'uses' chain, nearest declaration of a given check winning.
requires.title: Requires

max_failures.description: Max direct-subtask failures before independent subtasks are skipped. -1 or 0 = run all; 1 = stop on first; N > 1 = stop after N.
max_failures.title: Max Failures

on_error.description: Python callable (module:function) invoked as the compound's run hook when all direct subtasks complete.
on_error.title: On Error

TaskDef.title: TaskDef

uses.description: Base type to inherit from. Supports type extension/specialization
uses.title: Uses

with.description: Parameters for this type. Can be simple values or full parameter definitions
with.title: With

tags.description: Tags as type references with optional parameter overrides
tags.title: Tags

check.description: Python callable ('module:function') implementing this type as a graph-build CHECK, invoked for every node built from a task that `requires:` it. Signature: check(ctxt) -> None; report with ctxt.error()/ctxt.warning(). Inherited along the type's `uses:` chain.
check.title: Check
